lines.text: At one o'clock, the clock hands make a nice whole angle: thirty degrees.
lines.caption: At one o'clock, the clock hands make a nice whole angle: thirty degrees.

lines.text: One minute later, it's twenty-four and a half degrees. <short pause> That is not a whole number.
lines.caption: One minute later, it's twenty-four and a half degrees. That is not a whole number.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find out when it stays whole.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find out when it stays whole.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Look at every time from one o'clock to one fifty-nine, one minute apart.
lines.caption: Look at every time from one o'clock to one fifty-nine, one minute apart.

lines.text: At how many of these times is the smaller angle between the hands a whole number of degrees?
lines.caption: At how many of these times is the smaller angle between the hands a whole number of degrees?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So we have sixty times to check, from one o'clock to one fifty-nine.
lines.caption: So we have sixty times to check, from one o'clock to one fifty-nine.

lines.text: We count the times when the smaller angle is whole, like thirty, not twenty-four and a half.
lines.caption: We count the times when the smaller angle is whole, like thirty, not twenty-four and a half.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! The minute hand makes a full turn, three hundred sixty degrees, in sixty minutes.
lines.caption: Welcome back! The minute hand makes a full turn, three hundred sixty degrees, in sixty minutes.

lines.text: That's six degrees every minute.
lines.caption: That's six degrees every minute.

lines.text: The hour hand moves one number, thirty degrees, in sixty minutes. That's half a degree a minute.
lines.caption: The hour hand moves one number, thirty degrees, in sixty minutes. That's half a degree a minute.

lines.text: Now let's build a formula. Call the minutes past one o'clock m.
lines.caption: Now let's build a formula. Call the minutes past one o'clock m.

lines.text: At one o'clock, the hour hand points at the one. That's thirty degrees past the twelve.
lines.caption: At one o'clock, the hour hand points at the one. That's thirty degrees past the twelve.

lines.text: After m minutes, it has moved half a degree for each minute. So it's at thirty plus half of m.
lines.caption: After m minutes, it has moved half a degree for each minute. So it's at thirty plus half of m.

lines.text: The minute hand starts at the twelve. After m minutes, it's at six m.
lines.caption: The minute hand starts at the twelve. After m minutes, it's at six m.

lines.text: Every minute, the minute hand gains six minus a half. That's five and a half degrees per minute.
lines.caption: Every minute, the minute hand gains six minus a half. That's five and a half degrees per minute.

lines.text: So the gap between the hands is thirty minus five and a half m.
lines.caption: So the gap between the hands is thirty minus five and a half m.

lines.text: Let's test it at twenty past one. Thirty minus one hundred ten is minus eighty.
lines.caption: Let's test it at twenty past one. Thirty minus one hundred ten is minus eighty.

lines.text: A gap can't be negative, so the angle is eighty degrees.
lines.caption: A gap can't be negative, so the angle is eighty degrees.

lines.text: At forty past one, the gap is one hundred ninety. That's more than one hundred eighty.
lines.caption: At forty past one, the gap is one hundred ninety. That's more than one hundred eighty.

lines.text: So the smaller angle is three hundred sixty minus that: one hundred seventy degrees.
lines.caption: So the smaller angle is three hundred sixty minus that: one hundred seventy degrees.

lines.text: Now the big question. When is thirty minus five and a half m a whole number?
lines.caption: Now the big question. When is thirty minus five and a half m a whole number?

lines.text: Thirty is whole. So we need five and a half times m to be whole.
lines.caption: Thirty is whole. So we need five and a half times m to be whole.

lines.text: Five and a half times an even number is whole. Five and a half times two is eleven.
lines.caption: Five and a half times an even number is whole. Five and a half times two is eleven.

lines.text: An odd number leaves a half. Five and a half times three is sixteen and a half.
lines.caption: An odd number leaves a half. Five and a half times three is sixteen and a half.

lines.text: Three hundred sixty minus a whole number is whole too. So it's whole exactly when m is even.
lines.caption: Three hundred sixty minus a whole number is whole too. So it's whole exactly when m is even.

lines.text: Let's count the even minutes. Pair them up: zero and one, two and three, and so on.
lines.caption: Let's count the even minutes. Pair them up: zero and one, two and three, and so on.

lines.text: Sixty minutes make thirty pairs, with one even minute in each pair.
lines.caption: Sixty minutes make thirty pairs, with one even minute in each pair.

lines.text: So the answer is thirty. That's D!
lines.caption: So the answer is thirty. That's D!

lines.text: Here's a quicker way. Look at each hand on its own.
lines.caption: Here's a quicker way. Look at each hand on its own.

lines.text: The minute hand moves six degrees a minute, so it always sits on a whole degree.
lines.caption: The minute hand moves six degrees a minute, so it always sits on a whole degree.

lines.text: The hour hand starts at thirty and moves half a degree a minute.
lines.caption: The hour hand starts at thirty and moves half a degree a minute.

lines.text: On even minutes, it's on a whole degree. On odd minutes, it's on a half, like thirty and a half.
lines.caption: On even minutes, it's on a whole degree. On odd minutes, it's on a half, like thirty and a half.

lines.text: Whole minus whole is whole. But a whole number minus something and a half is never whole.
lines.caption: Whole minus whole is whole. But a whole number minus something and a half is never whole.

lines.text: So the angle is whole every other minute. Thirty times!
lines.caption: So the angle is whole every other minute. Thirty times!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When you want a fast answer without a formula.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When you want a fast answer without a formula.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Sixty counts every minute, without checking whether the angle is whole.
lines.caption: Sixty counts every minute, without checking whether the angle is whole.

lines.text: Twenty-nine counts the even minutes from two up to fifty-eight, and forgets one o'clock itself.
lines.caption: Twenty-nine counts the even minutes from two up to fifty-eight, and forgets one o'clock itself.

lines.text: Twelve is what you would get if you only counted times when the minute hand points right at a number.
lines.caption: Twelve is what you would get if you only counted times when the minute hand points right at a number.

lines.text: Fifteen is what you'd get if you counted only even angles. But odd ones, like nineteen, count too.
lines.caption: Fifteen is what you'd get if you counted only even angles. But odd ones, like nineteen, count too.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Check the very first time, and test an even minute AND an odd minute.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Check the very first time, and test an even minute AND an odd minute.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now the times run from two o'clock to two fifty-nine.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Now the times run from two o'clock to two fifty-nine.

lines.text: At how many of them is the smaller angle a multiple of five degrees, like five, ten or fifteen?
lines.caption: At how many of them is the smaller angle a multiple of five degrees, like five, ten or fifteen?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: At two o'clock, the hour hand is at sixty degrees. So the gap is sixty minus five and a half m.
lines.caption: At two o'clock, the hour hand is at sixty degrees. So the gap is sixty minus five and a half m.

lines.text: First, the angle must be whole, so m must be even.
lines.caption: First, the angle must be whole, so m must be even.

lines.text: Five and a half times an even minute gives eleven, twenty-two, thirty-three: multiples of eleven.
lines.caption: Five and a half times an even minute gives eleven, twenty-two, thirty-three: multiples of eleven.

lines.text: Sixty is a multiple of five. So we need a multiple of eleven that is ALSO a multiple of five.
lines.caption: Sixty is a multiple of five. So we need a multiple of eleven that is ALSO a multiple of five.

lines.text: That's zero, then fifty-five, then one hundred ten, and so on.
lines.caption: That's zero, then fifty-five, then one hundred ten, and so on.

lines.text: Fifty-five is five and a half times ten, so they come every ten minutes.
lines.caption: Fifty-five is five and a half times ten, so they come every ten minutes.

lines.text: Three hundred sixty minus a multiple of five is one too. So m is zero, ten, twenty, up to fifty.
lines.caption: Three hundred sixty minus a multiple of five is one too. So m is zero, ten, twenty, up to fifty.

lines.text: That's six times! Check ten past two: sixty minus fifty-five is five degrees.
lines.caption: That's six times! Check ten past two: sixty minus fifty-five is five degrees.

lines.text: If you found six, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found six, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea.

lines.text: Write the gap between the hands as a formula in the minutes: thirty minus five and a half m.
lines.caption: Write the gap between the hands as a formula in the minutes: thirty minus five and a half m.

lines.text: Then ask which minutes make it whole. Here, every even minute works.
lines.caption: Then ask which minutes make it whole. Here, every even minute works.
